column1: # voice_allow.tsv — front-facing files whose plural words are DATA, not voice.
# guard/voice_check.py keeps the FRONT-FACING prose first-person singular: README files,
# docs/, adopt/, specs/. Code is out of scope, and so is skills/ and templates/ — that
# material is written to be pulled into another fleet, where it becomes that team's own
# operating instructions and "we" is the adopting team speaking, not this author.
# This file is empty on purpose. It exists because a front-facing document could one day
# need to QUOTE plural language (an example of a phrasing to avoid, a quotation from
# someone else), and an exception with a stated reason is better than weakening the rule.
# Every line here is CHECKED: a file listed with no remaining matches is reported as a
# stale exemption, so the list cannot quietly widen. It reported all eight of its first
# entries the moment the scope narrowed, which is the behaviour to keep.
# Format:  PATH<TAB>why the words in this file are data rather than voice
